subject.title: Policy plugins cannot see resolved/served model identity at any blocking-capable hook (security impact: our confidentiality guard failed open)

question: Should OpenClaw extend `before_agent_run` with read-only resolved provider/model identity, add a new post-resolve blocking hook, or defer this to a broader guardrails API design?
rationale: The source-proven gap is security-relevant, but the exact hook shape changes a public plugin API and determines how much model-routing metadata trusted plugins can see before model submission.

options.title: Add identity to existing gate
options.body: Expose read-only resolved provider/model on `before_agent_run` or its context so existing block semantics can enforce per-turn model policy with the smallest new surface.

options.title: Add a post-resolve gate
options.body: Create a new blocking hook after model resolution and before provider submission, which is cleaner phase separation but adds another lifecycle hook contract.

options.title: Fold into guardrails design
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader guardrail-provider interface in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/72741, accepting that the specific confidentiality gap stays unresolved until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Add identity to existing gate
recommendation.body: Expose read-only resolved provider/model on `before_agent_run` or its context so existing block semantics can enforce per-turn model policy with the smallest new surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The current blocking gate came from this owner’s merged lifecycle-gate work, making them the best available routing candidate for the hook-shape decision.
